title: Set up a project through its tools: slicer init, matrix init, adj init and the adj flag
lead: *Proposed.* A daemon method `project.setup` and the command `ork projects setup NAME STEP [--dry-run] [--json]` run one setup step in a registered project through the owning tool: `slicer-init` (`slicer init`), `relay-roles-init` (`slicer relay-roles init --render`), `adj-init` (`adj init`, then the registry's `adj` flag on) and `adj-off` (the registry's `adj` flag off, no adj call). A dry run returns the exact command and runs nothing. This is the wire and CLI half; the TUI settings pane uses it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-11-02: ork should be able to set up a project end to end, UI first, also from the CLI and from AI workflows, without hand-editing files and without ork writing slicer's or adj's files (`docs/boundaries.md:75-79`). Today a newly added project that lacks `.slicer/` shows as "no slicer" (`ui.setup-errors`, adj 83) and the owner leaves ork to run `slicer init` and `slicer relay-roles init`. adj is on for a project only if `.adjudicate.json` existed when it was added: `addProject` stats it once (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:474-476`), and no command changes the `adj` flag afterwards (`projects.set` has no `adj` field, `internal/daemon/wire.go:271-286`; `docs/state.md:119-120`: "`name`, `path` and `adj` are set by `projects add`").

The owning commands exist and are safe to repeat or refuse cleanly:
- `slicer init [--force] ...` creates `.slicer/`; `--json` returns `{root, dir}` (`slicer/docs/commands.md:27`). ork never passes `--force`.
- `slicer relay-roles init` writes the example matrix and refuses an existing one without `--force` (exit 2, code `state`; `slicer/src/slicer/ops.py:3330-3338`). ork never passes `--force`.
- `adj init [--root DIR]`: "Safe to run again: an existing config and the records in the store are left as they are" (`adjudicate/internal/cli/init.go:11-17`); text only, exit 0.

The pattern for a write with no run record is `item.note` (`internal/daemon/items.go:34-49`: the slicer client with a zero `runrec.Writer{}`, slicer's error returned as it came). S173's `matrix.edit` uses the same pattern and the same `preview`/`command` shape; this slice follows it. Every write lands in the project's main checkout and stays uncommitted, as `matrix.edit` (owner, 2026-10-29).

Not here: `slicer setup-git` (it changes the clone's git config; an owner question), slicer `init` options such as `--id-prefix`, an adj contract pin (S206), the matrix's own edits (S173, S226 and the `matrix-apply` outline), any ork preferences profile (the owner decided on 2026-11-02 that each tool keeps its own store and no profile is built now).

Wire (*proposed*): `project.setup {project, step, preview?}` returns `{command, done, adj?}`. `command` is the line the owner confirms (`slicer init`, `slicer relay-roles init --render`, `adj init`, or `registry: adj off`), without `--json` or `--root`. `preview: true` runs nothing. `adj` is the registry flag after the step, for `adj-init` and `adj-off`. `adj-init` and `adj-off` change the registry under its lock and are refused with `project_busy` while the project has unfinished runs, like `projects.set` (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:586-593`). The slicer steps are not refused while runs are unfinished; slicer refuses what it refuses.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Clients:
- `TestSlicerInitArgv` and `TestRelayRolesInitArgv` (`internal/slicercli`): exactly `init --json --root ROOT` and `relay-roles init --render --json --root ROOT`; neither ever has `--force`. Fails first: no functions.
- `TestAdjInitArgv` (`internal/adjcli`): exactly `init --root ROOT`.

Daemon (`readDaemon`, `clitest.Route`):
- `TestProjectSetupPreviewRunsNothing`: each step with `preview: true` returns its `command` and `done: false`, and the fake records no call; the registry is unchanged.
- `TestProjectSetupSlicerInitRuns`: `slicer-init` makes one call and returns `done: true`. Fails first: unknown method.
- `TestProjectSetupRelayRolesInitPassesSlicersRefusal`: slicer exits 2 with `{"error":{"code":"state",...}}`: the same code and message come back.
- `TestProjectSetupAdjInitTurnsTheFlagOn`: `adj init` runs once, then the registry entry has `adj: true`, and the result has `adj: true`; a failing `adj init` leaves the flag as it was.
- `TestProjectSetupAdjOffMakesNoAdjCall`: `adj-off` sets `adj: false` with no tool call.
- `TestProjectSetupAdjStepsRefuseAnUnfinishedRun`: `project_busy`, no call, registry unchanged; `slicer-init` is not refused for that reason.
- `TestProjectSetupRefusesBadRequests`: missing project, unknown project (`not_found`), unknown step (`bad_params`, the message lists the four steps).
- `TestProjectSetupOverTheSocket`.

CLI:
- `TestProjectsSetupDryRunPrintsTheCommand`: `ork projects setup p adj-init --dry-run` prints `would run: adj init` and sends `preview: true`.
- `TestProjectsSetupRunsAndReports`: without `--dry-run` it prints `ran: adj init (adj on)`; `--json` prints the wire result.
- `TestProjectsSetupUsage`: a missing or unknown step is a usage error with no daemon call.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests; see each fail for the reason given.
2. Clients over the existing `write` helpers, with a zero `runrec.Writer{}` from the daemon.
3. Daemon: a step table (name, command text, run function, whether it changes the registry). Resolve the project with `d.registered`. The adj steps take the registry lock and the runs lock in the order `setProject` does and save with `registry.Save`. After a slicer or adj write, refresh the project's cache parts as `itemNote` does, so the Overview drops "no slicer".
4. Wire, dispatch, client, CLI.
5. Docs; CHANGELOG last.
6. Never pass `--force`; never open `.slicer/` or `.adjudicate.json`; do not touch `internal/tui`, `internal/engine`, or `projects.set`.

UI slice: UI pass (r14).
